metadata.title: A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems
metadata.venue: SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences, Vol. 2, No. 1, pp. 183-202

items.name: Positive part function
items.statement: For any real number $a$, the positive part is defined as $(a)_+ := \max\{a, 0\}$.

items.name: Shrinkage (soft-thresholding) operator
items.statement: For $\alpha > 0$, the shrinkage operator $T_\alpha : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is defined componentwise by $$T_\alpha(x)_i = (|x_i|-\alpha)_+ \operatorname{sgn}(x_i), \quad i = 1,\ldots,n.$$

items.name: $C^{1,1}$ function class (Lipschitz continuous gradient)
items.statement:
A function $f : \mathbb{R}^n 	o \mathbb{R}$ is of type $C^{1,1}$ if it is continuously differentiable and its gradient $
abla f$ is Lipschitz continuous with constant $L(f) > 0$: $$\|
abla f(x) - 
abla f(y)\| \le L(f)\|x-y\| \quad 	ext{for every } x,y \in \mathbb{R}^n,$$ where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the standard Euclidean norm and $L(f)$ is the Lipschitz constant of $
abla f$.

items.name: Subdifferential of a convex function
items.statement: For a convex function $g : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the subdifferential $\partial g(x)$ at a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of subgradients: $$\partial g(x) := \{\gamma \in \mathbb{R}^n : g(y) \ge g(x) + \langle \gamma, y-x\rangle \text{ for all } y \in \mathbb{R}^n\}.$$

items.name: General convex optimization model (Problem P)
items.statement:
The general nonsmooth convex optimization model is $$(\mathrm{P})\quad \min\{F(x) \equiv f(x) + g(x) : x \in \mathbb{R}^n\},$$ where:
- $g : \mathbb{R}^n 	o \mathbb{R}$ is a continuous convex function which is possibly nonsmooth.
- $f : \mathbb{R}^n 	o \mathbb{R}$ is a smooth convex function of type $C^{1,1}$, i.e., continuously differentiable with Lipschitz continuous gradient $L(f)$.
- Problem (P) is solvable, i.e., $X^* := \arg\min F 
e \emptyset$, and for $x^* \in X^*$ we set $F_* := F(x^*)$.

items.name: Quadratic approximation $Q_L(x,y)$
items.statement: For any $L > 0$, the quadratic approximation of $F(x) := f(x) + g(x)$ at a given point $y$ is $$Q_L(x,y) := f(y) + \langle x-y, \nabla f(y)\rangle + \frac{L}{2}\|x-y\|^2 + g(x).$$

items.name: Proximal operator $p_L(y)$
items.statement: For any $L > 0$ and $y \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the proximal operator (or prox-map) is defined as the unique minimizer $$p_L(y) := \arg\min\{Q_L(x,y) : x \in \mathbb{R}^n\}.$$ Equivalently, ignoring constant terms in $y$, $$p_L(y) = \arg\min_x \left\{ g(x) + \frac{L}{2}\left\|x - \left(y - \frac{1}{L}\nabla f(y)\right)\right\|^2 \right\}.$$

items.name: Descent Lemma (Quadratic upper bound for $C^{1,1}$ functions)
items.statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuously differentiable function with Lipschitz continuous gradient and Lipschitz constant $L(f)$. Then, for any $L \ge L(f)$, $$f(x) \le f(y) + \langle x-y, \nabla f(y)\rangle + \frac{L}{2}\|x-y\|^2 \quad \text{for every } x,y \in \mathbb{R}^n.$$
items.proof: Cited from: J. M. Ortega and W. C. Rheinboldt, Iterative Solution of Nonlinear Equations in Several Variables, Classics Appl. Math. 30, SIAM, Philadelphia, 2000; and D. P. Bertsekas, Nonlinear Programming, 2nd ed., Athena Scientific, Belmont, MA, 1999.

items.name: Lemma 2.1: Quadratic upper bound (Descent Lemma) for $C^{1,1}$ functions
items.statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuously differentiable function with Lipschitz continuous gradient and Lipschitz constant $L(f)$. Then, for any $L \ge L(f)$, $$f(x) \le f(y) + \langle x-y, \nabla f(y)\rangle + \frac{L}{2}\|x-y\|^2 \quad \text{for every } x,y \in \mathbb{R}^n.$$
items.proof: The quadratic upper bound follows from the Lipschitz continuity of the gradient by the standard descent-lemma argument.

items.name: Lemma 2.2: Optimality characterization of the proximal operator
items.statement: For any $y \in \mathbb{R}^n$, one has $z = p_L(y)$ if and only if there exists $\gamma(y) \in \partial g(z)$, the subdifferential of $g(\cdot)$, such that $$\nabla f(y) + L(z-y) + \gamma(y) = 0.$$
items.proof: The proof is immediate from optimality conditions for the strongly convex problem (2.6). Since $Q_L(\cdot, y)$ is strongly convex with modulus $L$, the first-order necessary and sufficient optimality condition is $0 \in \partial(Q_L(\cdot, y))(z) = \nabla f(y) + L(z-y) + \partial g(z)$.

items.name: Lemma 2.3: Key inequality for gradient-step analysis
items.statement: Let $y \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and $L > 0$ be such that $$F(p_L(y)) \le Q_L(p_L(y), y).$$ Then for any $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $$F(x) - F(p_L(y)) \ge \frac{L}{2}\|p_L(y)-y\|^2 + L\langle y-x, p_L(y)-y\rangle.$$
items.proof:
From (2.9), we have $F(x) - F(p_L(y)) \ge F(x) - Q_L(p_L(y), y)$.

Now, since $f,g$ are convex we have
$$f(x) \ge f(y) + \langle x-y, 
abla f(y)angle,$$
$$g(x) \ge g(p_L(y)) + \langle x-p_L(y), \gamma(y)angle,$$
where $\gamma(y)$ is defined in the premise of Lemma 2.2. Summing the above inequalities yields
$$F(x) \ge f(y) + \langle x-y, 
abla f(y)angle + g(p_L(y)) + \langle x-p_L(y), \gamma(y)angle.$$

On the other hand, by the definition of $p_L(y)$ one has
$$Q_L(p_L(y),y) = f(y) + \langle p_L(y)-y, 
abla f(y)angle +  rac{L}{2}\|p_L(y)-y\|^2 + g(p_L(y)).$$

Therefore, using the above inequalities it follows that
$$ egin{aligned}
F(x)-F(p_L(y))
&\ge - rac{L}{2}\|p_L(y)-y\|^2 + \langle x-p_L(y), 
abla f(y)+\gamma(y)angle \
&= - rac{L}{2}\|p_L(y)-y\|^2 + L\langle x-p_L(y), y-p_L(y)angle \
&=  rac{L}{2}\|p_L(y)-y\|^2 + L\langle y-x, p_L(y)-yangle,
\end{aligned}$$
where in the first equality above we used (2.8) from Lemma 2.2.

Note that from Lemma 2.1, it follows that if $L \ge L(f)$, then the condition (2.9) is always satisfied for $p_L(y)$.

items.name: Lemma 4.1: Key recursive relation for FISTA
items.statement: The sequences $\{x_k, y_k\}$ generated via FISTA with either a constant or backtracking stepsize rule satisfy for every $k \ge 1$, $$\frac{2}{L_k}t_k^2 v_k - \frac{2}{L_{k+1}}t_{k+1}^2 v_{k+1} \ge \|u_{k+1}\|^2 - \|u_k\|^2,$$ where $$v_k := F(x_k) - F(x^*), \qquad u_k := t_k x_k - (t_k-1)x_{k-1} - x^*.$$
items.proof:
First apply Lemma 2.3 at the points $(x := x_k, y := y_{k+1})$ with $L = L_{k+1}$, and likewise at the points $(x := x^*, y := y_{k+1})$, to get
$$2L_{k+1}^{-1}(v_k-v_{k+1}) \ge \|x_{k+1}-y_{k+1}\|^2 + 2\langle x_{k+1}-y_{k+1}, y_{k+1}-x_kangle,$$
$$-2L_{k+1}^{-1}v_{k+1} \ge \|x_{k+1}-y_{k+1}\|^2 + 2\langle x_{k+1}-y_{k+1}, y_{k+1}-x^*angle,$$
where we used the fact that $x_{k+1} = p_{L_{k+1}}(y_{k+1})$.

To get a relation between $v_k$ and $v_{k+1}$, we multiply the first inequality above by $(t_{k+1}-1)$ and add it to the second inequality:
$$ rac{2}{L_{k+1}} ig((t_{k+1}-1)v_k - t_{k+1}v_{k+1} ig) \ge t_{k+1}\|x_{k+1}-y_{k+1}\|^2 + 2\langle x_{k+1}-y_{k+1}, t_{k+1}y_{k+1}-(t_{k+1}-1)x_k-x^*angle.$$

Multiplying the last inequality by $t_{k+1}$ and using the relation $t_k^2 = t_{k+1}^2 - t_{k+1}$ which holds thanks to (4.2), we obtain
$$ rac{2}{L_{k+1}}(t_k^2 v_k - t_{k+1}^2 v_{k+1}) \ge \|t_{k+1}(x_{k+1}-y_{k+1})\|^2 + 2t_{k+1}\langle x_{k+1}-y_{k+1}, t_{k+1}y_{k+1}-(t_{k+1}-1)x_k-x^*angle.$$

Applying the Pythagoras relation $\|b-a\|^2 + 2\langle b-a, a-cangle = \|b-c\|^2 - \|a-c\|^2$ to the right-hand side with
$$a := t_{k+1}y_{k+1}, \qquad c := (t_{k+1}-1)x_k + x^*, \qquad b := t_{k+1}x_{k+1},$$
we get
$$ rac{2}{L_{k+1}}(t_k^2 v_k - t_{k+1}^2 v_{k+1}) \ge \|t_{k+1}x_{k+1} - (t_{k+1}-1)x_k - x^*\|^2 - \|t_{k+1}y_{k+1} - (t_{k+1}-1)x_k - x^*\|^2.$$

Therefore, with $y_{k+1}$ defined by $t_{k+1}y_{k+1} = t_{k+1}x_k + (t_k-1)(x_k-x_{k-1})$ (cf. (4.3)) and $u_k = t_k x_k - (t_k-1)x_{k-1} - x^*$, it follows that
$$ rac{2}{L_{k+1}}(t_k^2 v_k - t_{k+1}^2 v_{k+1}) \ge \|u_{k+1}\|^2 - \|u_k\|^2,$$
which combined with the inequality $L_{k+1} \ge L_k$ yields the desired result.

items.name: Lemma 4.2: Sequence inequality
items.statement: Let $\{a_k, b_k\}$ be positive sequences of reals satisfying $a_k - a_{k+1} \ge b_{k+1} - b_k$ for all $k \ge 1$, with $a_1 + b_1 \le c$, $c > 0$. Then $a_k \le c$ for every $k \ge 1$.
items.proof: The result follows by induction. From $a_k - a_{k+1} \ge b_{k+1} - b_k$, summing from $k=1$ to $n-1$ gives $a_1 - a_n \ge b_n - b_1$, i.e., $a_n \le a_1 + b_1 - b_n \le a_1 + b_1 \le c$, since $b_n > 0$.

items.name: Lemma 4.3: Lower bound on the FISTA sequence $\{t_k\}$
items.statement: The positive sequence $\{t_k\}$ generated in FISTA via $t_{k+1} = \frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}{2}$ with $t_1 = 1$ satisfies $t_k \ge \frac{k+1}{2}$ for all $k \ge 1$.
items.proof: The proof follows by induction. For $k=1$, $t_1 = 1 \ge 2/2 = 1$, true. Assume $t_k \ge (k+1)/2$. Then $t_{k+1} = \frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}{2} \ge \frac{1+\sqrt{1+4((k+1)/2)^2}}{2} = \frac{1+\sqrt{1+(k+1)^2}}{2} \ge \frac{1+\sqrt{(k+2)^2/4 \cdot 4}}{2} = \frac{1+(k+2)}{2} = \frac{k+3}{2}$, completing the induction.

items.name: FISTA with constant stepsize
items.statement: FISTA with constant stepsize: the sequences satisfy the proximal update and the momentum recurrences of equations (4.1)--(4.3).

items.name: FISTA with backtracking
items.statement: FISTA with backtracking: each trial proximal step satisfies the majorization test, and the smallest accepted exponent determines the next stepsize and momentum iterate.

items.name: ISTA with constant stepsize
items.statement: ISTA with constant stepsize: for every iteration k >= 1, x_k is the proximal point p_{L(f)}(x_{k-1}).

items.name: ISTA with backtracking
items.statement: ISTA with backtracking: each iterate is selected from the smallest accepted proximal trial under the paper majorization test.

items.name: Theorem 3.1: Global convergence rate of ISTA — $O(1/k)$
items.statement: Let $\{x_k\}$ be the sequence generated by ISTA with either constant stepsize ($x_k = p_{L(f)}(x_{k-1})$) or backtracking stepsize rule. Then for any $k \ge 1$, $$F(x_k) - F(x^*) \le \frac{\alpha L(f)\|x_0 - x^*\|^2}{2k} \quad \forall x^* \in X^*,$$ where $\alpha = 1$ for the constant stepsize setting and $\alpha = \eta$ for the backtracking stepsize setting.
items.proof:
Invoking Lemma 2.3 with $x = x^*$, $y = x_n$, and $L = L_{n+1}$, we obtain
$$ rac{2}{L_{n+1}}(F(x^*)-F(x_{n+1})) \ge \|x_{n+1}-x_n\|^2 + 2\langle x_n-x^*,x_{n+1}-x_nangle = \|x^*-x_{n+1}\|^2 - \|x^*-x_n\|^2,$$
which combined with the bound $L_{n+1} \le \alpha L(f)$ and the fact that $F(x^*)-F(x_{n+1})\le 0$ yields
$$ rac{2}{\alpha L(f)}(F(x^*)-F(x_{n+1})) \ge \|x^*-x_{n+1}\|^2-\|x^*-x_n\|^2.$$

Summing this inequality over $n=0,\ldots,k-1$ gives
$$ rac{2}{\alpha L(f)}\left(kF(x^*) - \sum_{n=0}^{k-1}F(x_{n+1})ight) \ge \|x^*-x_k\|^2-\|x^*-x_0\|^2.$$

Invoking Lemma 2.3 one more time with $x = y = x_n$ and $L = L_{n+1}$ yields
$$ rac{2}{L_{n+1}}(F(x_n)-F(x_{n+1})) \ge \|x_n-x_{n+1}\|^2.$$
Since $L_{n+1} \ge  eta L(f)$ and $F(x_n)-F(x_{n+1})\ge 0$, it follows that
$$ rac{2}{ eta L(f)}(F(x_n)-F(x_{n+1})) \ge \|x_n-x_{n+1}\|^2.$$

Multiplying the last inequality by $n$ and summing over $n=0,\ldots,k-1$, we obtain
$$ rac{2}{ eta L(f)}\sum_{n=0}^{k-1}\left(nF(x_n)-(n+1)F(x_{n+1})+F(x_{n+1})ight) \ge \sum_{n=0}^{k-1} n\|x_n-x_{n+1}\|^2,$$
which simplifies to
$$ rac{2}{ eta L(f)}\left(-kF(x_k)+\sum_{n=0}^{k-1}F(x_{n+1})ight) \ge \sum_{n=0}^{k-1} n\|x_n-x_{n+1}\|^2.$$

Adding the two summed inequalities with appropriate weights, we get
$$ rac{2k}{\alpha L(f)}(F(x^*)-F(x_k)) \ge \|x^*-x_k\|^2 +  rac{ eta}{\alpha}\sum_{n=0}^{k-1}n\|x_n-x_{n+1}\|^2 - \|x^*-x_0\|^2,$$
and hence it follows that
$$F(x_k)-F(x^*) \le  rac{\alpha L(f)\|x^*-x_0\|^2}{2k}.$$

items.name: Theorem 4.4: Global convergence rate of FISTA — $O(1/k^2)$
items.statement: Let $\{x_k\}$, $\{y_k\}$ be generated by FISTA with either constant or backtracking stepsize rule. Then for any $k \ge 1$, $$F(x_k) - F(x^*) \le \frac{2\alpha L(f)\|x_0 - x^*\|^2}{(k+1)^2} \quad \forall x^* \in X^*,$$ where $\alpha = 1$ for the constant stepsize setting and $\alpha = \eta$ for the backtracking stepsize setting.
items.proof:
Define the quantities
$$a_k :=  rac{2}{L_k}t_k^2 v_k, \qquad b_k := \|u_k\|^2, \qquad c := \|y_1 - x^*\|^2 = \|x_0 - x^*\|^2,$$
and recall (cf. Lemma 4.1) that $v_k := F(x_k) - F(x^*)$.

Then, by Lemma 4.1 we have for every $k \ge 1$
$$a_k - a_{k+1} \ge b_{k+1} - b_k,$$
and hence assuming that $a_1 + b_1 \le c$ holds true, invoking Lemma 4.2, we obtain that
$$ rac{2}{L_k}t_k^2 v_k \le \|x_0 - x^*\|^2,$$
which combined with $t_k \ge (k+1)/2$ (by Lemma 4.3) yields
$$v_k \le  rac{2L_k\|x_0 - x^*\|^2}{(k+1)^2}.$$

Utilizing the upper bound on $L_k$ given by $L_k \le \alpha L(f)$, the desired result follows.

Thus, all that remains is to prove the validity of the relation $a_1 + b_1 \le c$. Since $t_1 = 1$, and using the definition of $u_k$ given in Lemma 4.1, we have
$$a_1 =  rac{2}{L_1}t_1^2 v_1 =  rac{2}{L_1}v_1, \qquad b_1 = \|u_1\|^2 = \|x_1 - x^*\|^2.$$

Applying Lemma 2.3 to the points $x := x^*$, $y := y_1$ with $L = L_1$, we get
$$F(x^*) - F(p_{L_1}(y_1)) \ge  rac{L_1}{2}\|p_{L_1}(y_1)-y_1\|^2 + L_1\langle y_1-x^*, p_{L_1}(y_1)-y_1angle.$$

Thus,
$$ egin{aligned}
F(x^*) - F(x_1) &= F(x^*) - F(p_{L_1}(y_1)) \
&\ge  rac{L_1}{2}\|p_{L_1}(y_1)-y_1\|^2 + L_1\langle y_1-x^*, p_{L_1}(y_1)-y_1angle \
&=  rac{L_1}{2}\|x_1-y_1\|^2 + L_1\langle y_1-x^*, x_1-y_1angle \
&=  rac{L_1}{2}\{\|x_1-x^*\|^2 - \|y_1-x^*\|^2\}.
\end{aligned}$$

Consequently,
$$ rac{2}{L_1}v_1 \le \|y_1-x^*\|^2 - \|x_1-x^*\|^2;$$
that is, $a_1 + b_1 \le c$ holds true.
